text: Waste no more time arguing what a good man should be. Be one.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: That man lives badly who does not know how to die well.
author: Seneca

text: For it is not death or pain that is to be feared, but the fear of pain or death.
author: Epictetus

text: There is only one good, knowledge, and one evil, ignorance.
author: Socrates

text: Wonder is the feeling of a philosopher, and philosophy begins in wonder.
author: Plato

text: And happiness is thought to depend on leisure; for we are busy that we may have leisure, and make war that we may live in peace.
author: Aristotle

text: Only after Winter comes do we know that the pine and the cypress are the last to fade.
author: Confucius

text: Knowing others is intelligence; knowing yourself is true wisdom. Mastering others is strength; mastering yourself is true power.
author: Lao Tzu

text: If we have our own why in life, we shall get along with almost any how.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

text: Out of the crooked timber of humanity, no straight thing was ever made.
author: Immanuel Kant

text: Conquer anger with love, evil with good, meanness with generosity, and lies with truth.
author: Buddha

text: Neither love nor fire can subsist without perpetual motion; both cease to live so soon as they cease to hope, or to fear.
author: La Rochefoucauld
work: Reflections; or Sentences and Moral Maxims

text: When the force of desire for the Truth blossoms, selfish desires wither away, just like darkness vanishes before the radiance of the light of dawn.
author: Adi Shankara

text: Friends are as companions on a journey, who ought to aid each other to persevere in the road to a happier life.
author: Pythagoras

text: A free man thinks of death least of all things; and his wisdom is a meditation not of death but of life.
author: Baruch Spinoza

text: Why should there not be a patient confidence in the ultimate justice of the people? Is there any better or equal hope in the world?
author: Abraham Lincoln

text: Truth suffers no loss if a vehement youth fails in finding it, in the same way that virtue and religion suffer no detriment if a criminal denies them.
author: Friedrich Schiller

text: All men can see these tactics whereby I conquer, but what none can see is the strategy out of which victory is evolved.
author: Sun Tzu

text: That which is most excellent, and is most to be desired by all happy, honest and healthy-minded men, is dignified leisure.
author: Cicero

text: It belongs to the imperfection of everything human that man can only attain his desire by passing through its opposite.
author: Søren Kierkegaard

text: Most of the luxuries, and many of the so-called comforts of life, are not only not indispensable, but positive hindrances to the elevation of mankind.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: A diamond was laying in the street covered with dirt. Many fools passed by. Someone who knew diamonds picked it up.
author: Kabir

text: Let the future tell the truth and evaluate each one according to his work and accomplishments. The present is theirs; the future, for which I really worked, is mine.
author: Nikola Tesla

text: We must approach religion with reverence and with love, and our heart will stand up and say, this is truth, and this is untruth.
author: Swami Vivekananda

text: Humanity may endure the loss of everything: all its possessions may be torn away without infringing its true dignity; — all but the possibility of improvement.
author: Fichte

text: Time is the father of truth, its mother is our mind.
author: Giordano Bruno

text: The knowledge of past times and of the places on the earth is both an ornament and nutriment to the human mind.
author: Leonardo da Vinci
work: The Notebooks of Leonardo da Vinci

text: All true opinions are living, and show their life by being capable of nourishment; therefore of change. But their change is that of a tree — not of a cloud.
author: John Ruskin

text: Men never do good unless necessity drives them to it; but when they are free to choose and can do just as they please, confusion and disorder become rampant.
author: Niccolò Machiavelli

text: For such Truth as opposeth no man's profit nor pleasure is to all men welcome.
author: Thomas Hobbes

text: Art may make a suit of clothes; but nature must produce a man.
author: David Hume
